_comment: Doc-retrieval query set for #376, kubernetes repo.
Every gold anchor was read out of the actual file before being written here.
kubernetes has NO in-repo ADR/RFC corpus (KEPs live in kubernetes/enhancements), so
these target what it DOES document: the apiserver and client-go ARCHITECTURE.md files,
the kube-proxy nftables/ipvs READMEs, the kubelet plugin watcher, and cri-api.
expectPath: substring of the gold chunk's file path.
expectHeading: substring of the gold chunk's heading trail (case-insensitive).
A hit requires BOTH, so a lucky match on another section of the same file is not a hit.
The code and abstain arms are loaded from queries-seeded-k8s.json by category so they
stay identical to the existing baselines: literal/conceptual/cross are the code arm
(docs must not intrude), nonsense/salad are the abstain arm (docs must not answer).

queries.query: why does the apiserver use a watch cache instead of reading from etcd every time
at what point in the request flow is the body deserialized relative to authentication
how does the apiserver resolve conflicting concurrent writes
what is responsible for registering API groups and their storage strategy
how are long running streaming protocols like exec and attach handled
how is the apiserver assembled from delegated servers
how does the apiserver expose discovery and OpenAPI schemas
how does client-go surface warnings and apply client side rate limiting
when should I use a dynamic client instead of a typed client
how does server side apply work from the client library
what generates the typed clientsets informers and listers
what are the standard controller patterns for a workqueue based reconciler
how does client-go build its REST configuration
which netfilter hooks does kube-proxy attach to and at what priority
explain netfilter chains tables and traversal order
how do I add my own rules alongside kube-proxy nftables mode
how does the kubelet discover device plugins over a unix socket
what is the design of the ipvs based proxy mode
how is the container runtime interface API versioned across releases
how does the scheduler performance integration test harness work
